checked_claims.note: Harer duality identifying top-degree cohomology with Steinberg coinvariants (St tensor H^{tensor r})_G is standard, and Broaddus cyclicity of St as a Mod-module is true for a specific generator. The attempt however takes s to be the class of the standard ordered filling system a1,b1,...,ag,bg. Broaddus Remark 4.4 (and the companion chord-diagram calculation) shows that this standard 4g-gon/filling-system class is trivial in St; the actual cyclic generator is a different 0-filling system phi0. With s=0 the half-turn identity tau_i s=s is vacuous and the coinvariant argument never sees the odd-tensor representation. The sketch that chord-slides make every filling system a G-translate of the standard A therefore cannot be a proof of cyclicity. Handle half-turns fixing the genuine Broaddus generator (and the sign of that action on St) are not established. Consequently H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5})=0 is not proved.

For each forgetful f_j with r=6-j: fibre cohomology only in degrees 0,1; q=0 Leray term vanishes above base vcd; no differential enters or leaves the (d_{j-1},1) slot; residue SES 0->H->R_j->Q(-1)^{j-2}->0 is correct as VMHS; V_r(-1) has weight r+2 so H^{d_{j-1}} has weight floor 27 and Gr^W_26 vanishes; strictness of the coefficient LES yields a surjection on Gr^W_26 from the V_{r+1} term onto the middle. FND-0037 (connecting maps from Gr^W_26 of the weight-two quotient in degree d_{j-1}-1) alters kernels, not cokernels, once the same-degree Gr of the quotient vanishes; it does not kill this surjection claim.

Formal composite of the five confirmed Gr^W_26 surjections for j=6,5,4,3,2 yields a surjection Gr^W_26 H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) onto Gr^W_26 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q). This is only a conditional reduction pending source vanishing.

The implication 'source vanishes => W_26 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)=0' is valid (smooth DM stack with constant Q coefficients has weights >=26 in degree 26, so W_26=Gr^W_26). Source vanishing is not established (C1 failed), so the claim remains unresolved rather than confirmed or refuted as a statement.
Poincare duality W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) = W_26 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) matches FND-0001 / target dictionary (d=21). Zero is formally the empty direct sum of Q(8). Depends on unresolved C4.

finding_candidates.evidence: Broaddus, Homology of the curve complex and the Steinberg module of the mapping class group, Remark 4.4 and Theorem 4.2 / Corollary 4.3: standard gluing is trivial in St; a nonstandard phi0 generates St as a cyclic Mod-module. ATT-0043 argument markdown explicitly takes s=[A] for the standard system A and claims G-cyclicity and tau_i s=s.
finding_candidates.statement: The standard ordered 0-filling system of 2g arcs a1,b1,...,ag,bg (standard 4g-gon side identification) represents the zero class in the Steinberg module St of Mod_{g,1}/Mod_g. Broaddus cyclicity uses a different nontrivial generator phi0. Any top-degree vanishing argument that takes the standard filling-system class as a cyclic generator fixed by handle half-turns is vacuous and does not compute (St tensor V)_G.

strongest_attack: Load-bearing odd-tensor top-degree vanishing fails: the attempt's cyclic Steinberg generator is the standard a_i,b_i filling system, which Broaddus proves is the zero class in St, so handle half-turns fixing that class give no information about (St tensor H^{tensor 5})_G; the actual Broaddus generator is a different 0-filling system not shown to be fixed by half-turns with controlled sign. The forgetful-tower weight/Leray argument is only a correct conditional reduction Gr^W_26 H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{tensor 5}) twoheadrightarrow Gr^W_26 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q), not an unconditional proof that the exact target vanishes or is a sum of Q(8).
theorem_statement: The exact group W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), equivalently W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21), is a direct sum of Q(8); a disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this exact group.
